summary: Given the ambiguous "Add logging to the app so we can debug production issues" brief, Claude Code loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming, explicitly classified the task as architectural, ran a multi-question design dialogue, wrote a spec to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-16-browser-logging-design.md, presented it for review with no code written, and only began planning/implementation after my "looks good, go ahead".
reasoning: All five acceptance criteria were satisfied and verified both on-screen and on disk/log.

observations.description: The Codex approach/spec gate did not function: agent reported twice — 'the Codex approach gate ran but returned an empty response (the resolved codexPath is a stub build, 0.0.0-stub)' and 'the Codex spec gate ran but ... returned empty, so the spec went through without an independent Codex review'. The story says the codex-plugin-cc plugin IS installed, so the stub returning empty means the second-opinion gate provided no value this run (agent degraded gracefully and logged it to an ungated ledger 20260917T013155Z-30953-31010).
Claude Code start-up required manually clearing four dialogs (theme, security notes, folder trust, bypass-permissions) despite HOWTO claiming dialog-bypass state was seeded in the isolated $HOME.

The design was presented in chat in two long parts ('Does part 1 look right?', 'Does part 2 look right?') before the spec was written, so I had to approve three times in total; the first two approvals were effectively section sign-offs rather than the spec gate.
In the multi-select 'Tooling' question, reaching 'Submit' required arrowing down past all options; there was no obvious shortcut, and 'Type something' sat between the last option and Submit.
Spec file was written but deliberately not committed ('not committed', git status shows '?? docs/'), which is fine but means the spec is not yet under version control at approval time.

criteria.evidence: grep of session log: `grep -o '"\(hyper\|super\)powers:[a-z-]*"' *.jsonl | sort | uniq -c` returned `36 "hyperpowers:brainstorming"`; screen also showed Skill(hyperpowers:writing-plans) only after approval.

criteria.criterion: Classified as ARCHITECTURAL and wrote spec to docs/.../specs/ before presenting design
criteria.evidence: Screen: 'Classification: architectural. "Add logging so we can debug production issues" asks for a logging subsystem this repo doesn't have...' and later 'Spec written to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-16-browser-logging-design.md'. Verified on disk: `ls docs/hyperpowers/specs/` → `2026-09-16-browser-logging-design.md`, head shows '# Browser Logging Subsystem — Design ... Status: awaiting review'.

criteria.criterion: Spec presented for review and approval before any implementation code
criteria.evidence: Screen: 'Please review it and let me know if you want any changes before we move on to the implementation plan. ... No code has been written.' git status at that moment showed only `?? docs/` with app.js/index.html/package.json unmodified (git log HEAD still 73d1374 'Add simple webapp fixture').

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as bounded / skip spec
criteria.evidence: Agent explicitly said 'this isn't a bounded one-file change, even though the first edit would land in app.js' and produced a committed-to-disk spec file rather than an in-chat-only design.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as spike / throwaway probe plan
criteria.evidence: No probe or spike language appeared; the flow was clarifying questions → 3 approaches (A/B/C) → sectioned design → spec doc → writing-plans skill. Screen after approval: 'Spec approved. Per the brainstorming skill, the next and only step is writing-plans.'
